title: Interest Rate for Early-Closing Interest on Credit Builder Accounts of Borrowers in Hardship Assistance Programs
content:
The rate at which closing interest is charged at an early closing of a Credit Builder account depends on the borrower's Larkspur hardship plans: the borrower's Hardship Assistance Programs plans, read from the hardship plan records (each plan's status, its program and its plan interest rate).

## Rate selection

- When the borrower has a Larkspur hardship plan in active status under the Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit, the closing interest uses the lower of the APR and that plan's interest rate.
- When the borrower has no such benefit but has a Larkspur hardship plan in active status under the Temporary Rate Reduction Plan, the closing interest uses that plan's interest rate instead of the APR.
- When the borrower has neither, the closing interest uses the APR.

The APR is the Credit Builder account's fixed APR. The rate chosen here is the rate the loan balance is charged at for the interest days.

| Borrower's active Hardship Assistance Programs plans | Rate for closing interest |
|---|---|
| a Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit | the lower of the APR and that plan's interest rate |
| a Temporary Rate Reduction Plan, no Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit | that plan's interest rate, whether above or below the APR |
| neither (other programs only, or no active plan) | the APR |

## Rates in practice (hypothetical figures)

With an APR of 15.00: an active Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit at 6.00 gives 6.00; one at 18.00 gives 15.00; an active Temporary Rate Reduction Plan at 8.00, with no Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit, gives 8.00; a borrower whose only active plan is a Term Extension Modification is charged 15.00.
